ishwaripur-hammamkhana.desc: In Ishwaripur, a small cluster of domed brick rooms is known locally as the Hammamkhana, an old bathhouse. Local tradition links it with the time of Raja Pratapaditya and the Mughal campaigns in the region. It is modest and little visited, but it hints at how important this now-quiet corner once was. Pair it with the nearby temple.
blocks: How to get there
Walk or take a van from the Jeshoreshwari temple; ask locals for the Hammamkhana.
Good to know
There are no facilities; carry water.

glance: Forest Department fee plus boat hire, approx.
kalagachhia-eco-tourism.desc: Kalagachhia is a Forest Department visitor spot inside the western Sundarbans. A wooden trail runs through the mangroves on stilts, and a watchtower looks over the canopy and channels. Monkeys are common, and kingfishers and egrets work the creek banks. It is the most practical short trip into the forest from the Satkhira side.
blocks: How to get there
Hire a boat from Burigoalini or Munshiganj; the ride takes roughly an hour depending on tide.
Good to know
Buy entry at the forest station first. Stay on the walkway, keep bags closed against monkeys, and return before dark.

glance: 240 km to Satkhira by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
tetulia-jami-mosque.desc: In Tetulia village in Tala upazila, Khan Bahadur Qazi Salamatullah of the local zamindar family built a six-domed Mughal-style mosque in 1858–59. Close by are the remains of his mansion, Salam Manzil, once known for its long twin-pillared verandah and a palanquin so big it needed twelve bearers. The mansion's gateway has been rebuilt, but the rest is now mostly in ruins. The mosque is still in use and is the main reason to come; the village setting makes it a peaceful detour.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Satkhira to Tala (about 1 hour), then an easy bike or van to Tetulia village.
Good to know
Ask for 'Tetulia Shahi Masjid'. Visit outside prayer times, and do not climb on the mansion ruins.

glance: 240 km to Satkhira by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
nakipur-zamindar-bari.desc: In Nakipur, the main settlement of Shyamnagar upazila, zamindar Haricharan Roy Chowdhury built his estate in the mid-1800s. It has a two-storey L-shaped building about 19 metres long with open verandahs, a pair of Shiva temples, a nahabatkhana (music gallery), a puja pavilion, a dispensary, and ponds. Locals still call it Roy Chowdhury bari, and tell that his mother dreamed of where sacks of treasure lay hidden. Neglect has left both the house and the temples close to ruin. It is right on the way to Munshiganj and the Sundarbans.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Satkhira to Shyamnagar (about 2 hours); the zamindar bari is in Nakipur near the H.C. Pilot High School, a short rickshaw or van ride.
Good to know
Ask for 'Haricharan Royer bari' or 'Roy Chowdhury bari'. The buildings are fragile, so look from outside and do not climb.

glance: 240 km to Satkhira by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
prabajpur-shahi-mosque.desc: This four-domed mosque stands in Prabajpur village, about four kilometres from Kaliganj upazila town. It was completed in 1693 in Aurangzeb's reign, and the village takes its name from Prabaj Khan, the commander credited with building it for Mughal troops stationed here. The red-brick building has three ornate mihrabs and once had ten doorways. The Department of Archaeology has protected it since 1968, and it remains a working mosque. Locals tell that jinns built it overnight and that vows made here come true.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Satkhira to Kaliganj (about 1 hour), then an easy bike or van about 4 km to Prabajpur.
Good to know
Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. Easy to combine with a trip south towards Shyamnagar and the Sundarbans.

bonbibi-puja.desc: In villages along the Sundarbans edge, people who fish, collect honey or cut golpata believe in Bonbibi, a protective forest spirit. Small shrines show her with her brother Shah Jangali and the tiger demon Dakkhin Rai. Both Hindu and Muslim families make offerings to her. Songs and plays retelling her story are still performed in winter, especially around Bengali month Magh.
blocks: Good to know
Shrines appear in villages near Munshiganj; ask politely before visiting during rituals.

glance: 240 km to Satkhira by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
Forest Department permit and fees, plus boat hire or a tour package
mandarbaria-beach.desc: Mandarbaria beach lies in the Sundarbans at the far south of Shyamnagar, beside the forest of the same name and the mouth of the Hariabhanga river, which marks the border with India. It is the longest beach inside the Bangladeshi Sundarbans, with mangrove forest at one end and open sea in front. There are no buildings, stalls or crowds; you may see crab trails, birds and deer tracks on the sand. Few people come because it can only be reached on a long boat trip with a forest permit.
blocks: How to get there
Only by boat. Go from Satkhira to Shyamnagar and on to Munshiganj or Burigoalini, then join a licensed tour or hire a trawler with a forest permit and guide.
Good to know
Travel only with a permit, an armed forest guard where required, and a licensed boat. Check the weather and avoid cyclone season; carry water and food, as there is nothing on the beach.

glance: 240 km to Satkhira by road, 6–8 hours by bus or car
Forest Department permit and boat hire required for forest entry
munshiganj-burigoalini.desc: Munshiganj and the Burigoalini forest station face the mangroves across the Chunar and Kholpetua rivers. From here boats head into the western Sundarbans for day trips and longer cruises. The villages themselves show coastal life up close, with crab ponds, salt-tolerant farming and boatyards. Evenings on the embankment, looking across at the forest, are calm and lovely.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Satkhira town to Shyamnagar (about 2 hrs), then local transport to Munshiganj or Burigoalini.
Good to know

Forest entry needs a Forest Department permit, issued through the Burigoalini station or arranged by a licensed operator, plus an armed guard for deeper trips. Do not swim or wander off trails; tigers and crocodiles live here. Check weather warnings during cyclone season.

jeshoreshwari-kali-temple.desc: The Jeshoreshwari temple at Ishwaripur in Shyamnagar is counted among the Shakti Peeths, sites sacred to the goddess. The present structure is associated with the era of Raja Pratapaditya, who ruled this region in the late 16th century. Pilgrims arrive especially during Kali Puja. Ruins from the same period lie nearby in the village.
blocks: How to get there
From Shyamnagar upazila town, a short auto or van ride to Ishwaripur.
Good to know
Remove shoes and ask before photographing inside the shrine.

glance: Bazars and hotels in Shyamnagar and Munshiganj
satkhira-crab.desc: The saline coast of Shyamnagar and Assasuni has turned to crab and shrimp farming, much of it for export. Mud crabs are fattened in small ponds and sold live in local markets. Cooked as a hot, thick curry, crab is a treat for visitors from inland. Tiger prawns are equally common on local menus.

glance: Approx. 80–150 BDT per kg in season
Satkhira town fruit markets and orchards in Kalaroa and Satkhira Sadar
satkhira-mango.desc: Thanks to its warm south-western location, Satkhira's mangoes ripen earlier than those of the northern belt. Himsagar, with its smooth fiberless flesh, is the favourite, and Langra and Amrapali follow. Orchards and roadside markets fill with fruit from late May. Satkhira mangoes are also among those exported abroad.

glance: Fakir Mistanna Bhander on Nazmul Sarani and Sagar Mistanna Bhander at Hotel Sagar, Shahid Kajal Sarani, Satkhira town
satkhira-sandesh.desc: Satkhira is one of the country's big milk districts, and its sweet makers are known nationwide; sandesh is the one they are proudest of. Fresh chhana is cooked with sugar, or in winter with new date gur, which most locals prefer. Fakir Mistanna Bhander, founded in 1947, is the oldest-known name in town, and Sagar Mistanna Bhander is famous for sandesh and swarpuri. In Kalaroa, the Ghosh families of Ghoshpara village still make sandesh by hand over wood fires.
blocks: Good to know
Ask for gur sandesh between December and February.
